idiom_name: class or interface with a readonly id; branded id types restore nominal identity
implementation_notes: TypeScript's runtime identity is JavaScript's reference identity (=== on objects), but its type system is structural, so two different entity types with the same shape are mutually assignable and a CustomerId is just a string - that is the local problem the pattern has to solve here. The idiom is to make identity explicit in the type system: define the entity with a readonly id, give the id a branded type built from a unique symbol intersection so a CustomerId cannot be passed where an OrderId is expected, and compare entities through that id (or with === while one instance per entity is guaranteed in memory). Serialization still destroys reference identity, so code that reconstitutes entities from JSON must reconcile by id, typically in a repository or store keyed by id.
pitfalls: Structural typing accepts any object with an id field where a Customer is expected; brand the id and parse at the boundary or ids of different entities stay interchangeable at compile time.
JSON.parse produces plain objects with no identity: after a round-trip === is false and methods are gone, so reconcile by id in the store instead of comparing deserialized copies.
Casting an arbitrary string with as CustomerId bypasses validation; brand only inside a validating constructor or schema (zod, io-ts) rather than at every call site.
